# Audit Scan

**IMPORTANT: This is a READ-ONLY command. Do not edit/write any code files. Do not
create tickets — that's the job of the separate `/caf-audit-to-ticket` command.**

Follow the same scope and rules as the agent definition in
`.claude/agents/caf-auditor.md` — if that file exists, read and follow it
as the primary source of truth. If it doesn't exist, use these default
principles: tools limited to Read + read-only Bash (`ls`, `grep`, `git blame`) plus Write
ONLY for saving the report to `.caf/audits/`; no write access to code
or to external systems (Linear, Jira, GitHub, etc).

## Scope

Audit target: $ARGUMENTS

If the argument is empty or contains "all modules", run a full scan across
the entire application (detect the structure first from package.json/workspace
config before starting — don't assume folder names without verifying).

## What to Look For

**Functional bugs (from code behavior, not assumptions):**
- Logic that is inconsistent with existing documentation/ADR/golden-example
- Edge cases that appear unhandled (missing null/undefined check on a path that clearly
  needs it, silent-swallow error handling with no log)
- API contract that changed but its consumers (frontend/other service) haven't been updated

**Tech debt:**
- Duplicated logic that should be shared (violates a documented golden-example pattern)
- Code that deviates from ADR conventions without a documented reason
- TODO/FIXME comments that have gone stale (check comment age via `git blame`)

**Performance (indications from static code, not runtime profiling):**
- Query inside a loop (N+1 pattern)
- An index that is clearly needed from frequently-used query patterns but doesn't exist
- Clearly excessive response payload (e.g. selecting all columns when only 2 are used)

**Out of scope for the CAF Auditor — DO NOT scan:**
- Deep security scanning (secrets, injection, auth bypass) is OUT OF SCOPE for the CAF Auditor (see CAF.md § Cluster 4) — that is the responsibility of a separate security review. If a serious security indication is hit incidentally, write it under `## Notes` for human attention; do not turn it into a priority finding and do not turn it into a ticket via this path.

**Routing rule: sensitive-data-exposure (applies across categories).**

Before placing a finding into "Priority Findings" or "Non-Priority Findings", check: does this finding
involve EXPOSURE of sensitive data/credentials (password/password_hash, token, secret, API key,
session secret, or PII that should not be public) — whether found through a functional bug scan,
tech debt, or performance scan?

If YES — regardless of its original category (`BUG` / `PERFORMANCE` / `TECH_DEBT` / `COVERAGE`) — move it to
`## Notes` § `### Sensitive Data Exposure`, NOT to Priority
Findings/Non-Priority Findings. This is not a new category: the original category classification is
still written down, only the handling route changes.

Write just enough description to be actionable (file/line location, type of data leaked,
original category) WITHOUT including the actual exposed value/payload.

Findings in this subsection are NOT converted into tickets by `/caf-audit-to-ticket` — they are
treated the same as other out-of-scope security indications. A human decides the handling route
outside the normal tracker.

Use judgment for other patterns relevant to the project's domain (check CLAUDE.md and
incident/hotfix history if available), but DO NOT assign a severity without including
supporting line-level evidence.

## Output Format

Output structure MUST match `.claude/agents/caf-auditor.md` (see the
`## Report Format` section in that file) so it can be parsed by `/caf-audit-to-ticket` (which
looks for the `## Priority Findings` heading and ignores
`## Non-Priority Findings` and all of `## Notes`):

```markdown
## Audit: <DATE>
## Agent: audit-scan (command)
## Scope: <original argument>

## Summary

<1-2 sentence summary of the state of the scanned area>

## Priority Findings

### 1. [CATEGORY] <short title>
- **Location:** `path/to/file.ext:line`
- **Category:** `BUG` / `PERFORMANCE` / `TECH_DEBT` / `COVERAGE`
- **Severity:** Critical / Moderate
- **Issue:** <concrete description, why this is a problem>
- **Impact:** <consequence if left unaddressed>
- **Suggestion:** <short direction for a fix, not a full implementation>

### 2. ...

## Non-Priority Findings (recorded, not proposed as tasks)

- <category, file:line location, severity Minor — short list, no detail>

## Notes

<things that need human attention — e.g. needs an architectural decision, requested scope
turned out to be broader than can be covered, or a security indication that falls outside
the Auditor's scope>

### Sensitive Data Exposure

<sensitive data/credential exposure findings, regardless of original category — leave empty if none>

- **Location:** `path/to/file.ext:line`
- **Original Category:** `BUG` / `PERFORMANCE` / `TECH_DEBT` / `COVERAGE`
- **Exposed Data:** <type of data only, e.g. "password hash in endpoint response" —
  DO NOT write the actual value/payload>
- **Issue:** <short description>
```

Severity Critical / Moderate → Priority Findings; Minor → Non-Priority
Findings. Group findings by module/area within each section. Sensitive-data-exposure
findings go under `## Notes` § `### Sensitive Data Exposure`
(full rule in the "What to Look For" section).

Different from `auditor.md`: **Priority Findings are NOT capped at N**.
The Auditor agent caps at 5 because it scans the whole repo (to control the AI run
budget on the weekly scan); this command is scoped to the area the user explicitly
requested, so every genuine finding of severity Critical / Moderate found in that
scope goes into Priority Findings.

Don't produce detailed implementation recommendations in this command — that's
outside the scope of a read-only audit.

## Save the Result

You MUST write the audit result to a file, NOT just display it in chat.

Location: `.caf/audits/<DATE>/audit-report-{scope-slug}.md`
- `<DATE>`: today's date, format YYYY-MM-DD (folder per date, same
  convention as the `auditor.md` agent)
- `{scope-slug}`: derived from the given argument, simplified to
  lowercase-kebab-case (e.g. "apps/web/src/modules/auth" becomes
  "auth-module"; "all modules" becomes "full-scan")

The filename is deliberately NOT plain `audit-report.md` — that name is reserved for
the output of the `auditor.md` agent (full-repo scan). This command is scoped, so always
use the `-{scope-slug}` suffix so it never collides with the agent's file.

If the `.caf/audits/<DATE>/` folder doesn't exist yet, create it.

**If `.caf/audits/<DATE>/audit-report-{scope-slug}.md` already exists**
(re-running the same scope on the same date): do NOT silently overwrite it.
APPEND a new section to the same file, with a clear separator:

```markdown

---

## Additional Scan: <HH:MM>
## Scope: <original argument>

## Summary
...
## Priority Findings
...
## Non-Priority Findings
...
```

Tell the user in chat that the result was appended to the existing file
(mention how many sections already exist in that file), not overwriting the
findings from the previous run.

After the file is saved, still show a summary in chat (number of findings
per severity), but tell the user the full file path so it can be
referenced later — including by `/caf-audit-to-ticket`.

Verify: confirm the file was actually written at the stated path
(check with Read or ls), not just claim "saved".

## After Finishing

Suggest to the user that they run `/caf-audit-to-ticket` if they want to convert
these findings into tickets (with per-item approval, not auto-create).

  Read audit-report.md produced by the Auditor Agent, display each finding for
  human approval one at a time, then create tickets ONLY for approved ones.
  Never auto-creates without explicit per-item confirmation.

## Context

You're running the human-in-the-loop step after the Auditor Agent finishes its scan.
The Auditor Agent is DELIBERATELY not allowed to create tickets itself (see
`.claude/agents/caf-auditor.md` § Scope: "that's a human decision, not this agent's"). This command is the sole official path from audit-report.md to Linear — don't create another one.

## Argument

`$ARGUMENTS` — optional, path to a specific audit file (e.g.
`.caf/audits/2026-07-10/audit-report.md` from the `auditor` agent, or
`.caf/audits/2026-07-10/audit-report-{scope-slug}.md` from
`/caf-audit-scan`). If empty, look for the most recent date folder in `.caf/audits/`.

## Steps

### 1. Find and read the audit file

- If `$ARGUMENTS` is empty: `ls -t .caf/audits/` to find the most recent date
  folder, then `ls .caf/audits/<DATE>/` to see all
  `audit-report*.md` files in it (there can be more than one: `audit-report.md`
  from the `auditor` agent full-scan, and/or `audit-report-{scope-slug}.md`
  from `/caf-audit-scan`).
  - If there's exactly 1 file → read it directly.
  - If there's more than 1 file → show the list to the user (filename +
    scope from each file's header) and ask the user to pick one (or
    process all of them in sequence if the user explicitly asks). DO NOT
    assume which file is meant.
- If there's no `audit-report*.md` file at all in the most recent date
  folder, report this to the user and STOP — don't continue with any assumption.
- Parse ALL "## Priority Findings" sections in the selected file — the file may
  contain more than one such section if `/caf-audit-scan` was run multiple times
  on the same day for the same scope (results are appended, not overwritten; see
  "## Additional Scan" as the separator between runs). Combine all findings from
  each "## Priority Findings" section found into a single list to
  process. Ignore "## Non-Priority Findings" in any section (deliberately
  not proposed as tasks by the Auditor).
- Also ignore the ENTIRE contents of "## Notes" — including the
  "### Sensitive Data Exposure" subsection. That content is deliberately routed
  outside the ticket path (see Constraints below).
- If a finding under "## Priority Findings"/"## Non-Priority Findings"
  turns out to be about exposure of sensitive data/credentials
  (password/password_hash, token, secret, API key, session secret, PII that
  shouldn't be public) — meaning it slipped past the Auditor's filter — DO NOT
  process it into a ticket. Report to the user that this finding was skipped
  because it belongs in "## Notes" § "### Sensitive Data Exposure",
  without quoting the exposed value/payload.

### 2. Show each finding one at a time, ask for an explicit decision

For EVERY finding in "Priority Findings", show it to the user exactly as
below and WAIT for an answer before moving to the next finding — don't process
in batch without per-item confirmation:

```
---
Finding N/TOTAL: [CATEGORY] <title>
Location: <file:line>
Problem: <description from audit-report.md>
Impact: <from audit-report.md>
Proposal: <from audit-report.md>

Turn this into a ticket? (yes / edit / skip)
---
```

- **yes** → proceed to step 3 with the description as-is from audit-report.md
- **edit** → ask which part to change (title/description/severity), then
  confirm the edited version before proceeding to step 3
- **skip** → record as "not created", move to the next finding

### 3. Create Linear issue (only for approved items)

- Use `mcp__linear__listTeams` if the team ID isn't already known from project context.
- Title: finding title (concise, actionable — not a copy-paste of a long description)
- Description: the following format, filled in from audit-report.md (or the edited version):
  ```
  ## Source
  Auditor Agent scan <audit date>, file: `.caf/audits/<date>/audit-report.md`

  ## Location
  <file:line>

  ## Problem
  <description>

  ## Impact
  <impact>

  ## Proposal
  <proposed task>
  ```
- Label/priority: map from category (first check which labels actually exist in the workspace
  via `mcp__linear__listLabels`, don't assume they exist) —
  - `BUG` → priority High, label `bug`
  - `PERFORMANCE` → priority Medium, label `performance`
  - `TECH_DEBT` → priority Medium, label `tech-debt`
  - `COVERAGE` → priority Low-Medium, label `test-coverage`
- Save the issue ID + URL returned by Linear.

### 4. Final summary

After all findings have been processed, show a summary:

```
Done. Out of N priority findings:
- X turned into tickets: [list of titles + link/number]
- Y skipped: [short list of titles]
- Z edited before creation: [list of titles]
```

## Constraints (must not be violated)

- DO NOT create an issue without explicit per-item confirmation — "yes" for one
  finding does not mean "yes" for all.
- DO NOT process "Non-Priority Findings" (severity Minor) — these are
  deliberately not proposed by the Auditor. Only Critical / Moderate are processed.
- Valid finding categories are only `BUG` / `PERFORMANCE` / `TECH_DEBT` / `COVERAGE`. Deep security scanning (secrets, injection, auth bypass) is OUT OF SCOPE for the CAF Auditor (see CAF.md § Cluster 4) — that is the responsibility of a separate security review. If a serious security indication is hit incidentally, write it under `## Notes` for human attention; do not turn it into a priority finding and do not turn it into a ticket via this path.
- DO NOT create a ticket for findings involving exposure of sensitive data/credentials
  (password/password_hash, token, secret, API key, session secret, PII that shouldn't be
  public) — regardless of its original category (`BUG` / `PERFORMANCE` / `TECH_DEBT` / `COVERAGE`), and regardless of the
  section it appears in. Route it to "## Notes" § "### Sensitive Data Exposure"
  for a human decision outside the tracker. Judge by the substance of the finding, not by
  string-matching field names.
- DO NOT edit/delete audit-report.md — that file belongs to the Auditor Agent, this
  command is read-only with respect to it.
- DO NOT create a `.caf/tasks/<TICKET-ID>/` folder — that's the Planner Agent's domain
  once the ticket enters the normal pipeline, not this command's responsibility.
- If the Linear MCP fails (auth, rate limit, etc) mid-process, STOP and report
  progress so far (don't retry silently, don't continue to the next finding
  as if everything is fine).

# Complete CAF Drafts

This repo was scaffolded with `caf-init`. The generated files are drafts full of `TODO`s. Your job
is to complete them so the CAF agents (planner, implementation, QA, reviewer) work from correct
context.

**The rule that governs everything below:** these documents are read by agents as the truth on
every ticket, so one wrong claim gets repeated forever. An honest, incomplete document is worth
more than a complete, invented one. If you cannot prove something from the contents of this repo,
leave the `TODO` and ask the user.

## Project shape (detected when this command was generated)

This is a **single-package repo** (`SINGLE_REPO`): one package at the repo root (`website-cms-v2`, framework detected: Nuxt), no workspaces.
Package manager: `pnpm`.
Verification commands are the root `package.json` scripts, run unscoped.

Re-check these against the repo in step 1 — detection can be stale. If the repo contradicts it,
trust the repo and tell the user.

## Drafts found at generation time

- `.claude/agents/caf-architect.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-auditor.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-documentation.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-implementer.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-planner.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-pm.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-qa.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`
- `.claude/agents/caf-ux-designer.md`

## Arguments

`$ARGUMENTS` — optional, limit the work to one file or area. If empty, cover every draft above
plus any `docs/` reference document that exists.

## Steps

### 1. Read — do not write anything yet

- The code: `package.json` (every workspace's, in a monorepo), framework config, folder layout, a
  few representative files in each main folder, test setup, lint/format config, CI config, README.
- Every draft listed above, plus `.caf/**`, `.claude/agents/*.md` and `docs/**` as they are now.

### 2. Report the plan and your questions — then STOP

Tell the user:
- which files you will fill and which parts you can prove from the code,
- which parts are human decisions (see "Never invent" below), as specific questions grouped per
  document so they can be answered briefly.

**STOP here and wait for the user's answers.** Do not start writing until they reply. A question
they leave unanswered stays a `TODO` (or becomes an explicit open question in the document).

### 3. Fill in the drafts

#### Fill directly from the code — every claim must point at a real file

`CLAUDE.md`
- **Verification Commands**: only scripts that actually exist in `package.json`, by their exact
  names. If typecheck/lint/test has no script of its own, record that as a gap — never write a
  command that does not exist.
- **Code Conventions**: patterns that are genuinely consistent in the code (folder structure,
  naming, API calls, error/loading handling, state, styling), specific to this project — not
  general framework advice. Where the code is inconsistent, say so and ask which pattern is right.
- **Database**: what the repo actually shows. If this repo has no database of its own, say that.
- Keep the file under roughly 150 lines.

`AGENTS.md`
- **Concrete Rules**: 3–6 rules visible in the code, each with a right example taken from a real
  file (cite its path) and a realistic wrong example.

`.claude/agents/*.md`
- Fill only `## Role`, `## Scope` and `## Verify Checklist`, and only where a `TODO` remains.
- Leave a `## Skills` section exactly as it is — its pointers are managed by
  `caf-init scaffold skills`. Do not add, remove or reorder them.
- **Do NOT change** `## Allowed Tools`, `## Input`, `## Output`, `## Working Pattern (PIV)`, `## Retry Logic`, `## What to Look For`, `## Report Format`, or the frontmatter. These sections are tracked by
  `caf-init curate`: an edit there stops future template fixes from reaching this file, and
  their report/status formats are parsed word-for-word by caf-orchestrator.
- Leave every `TODO` about MCP servers alone — that is a security decision for a human.

`.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` (CAF skills)
- Glob `.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md` **now** — skills can be added after this command was generated,
  so the list of drafts above is not the source for them.
- Work only on a skill that still starts with a `DRAFT` banner. A skill without the banner is
  finished: do not edit it.
- In a DRAFT skill, replace a line that starts with `TODO` only with a command whose script
  really exists in `package.json` (exact name, scoped to its workspace in a monorepo). If no such
  script exists, say so to the user and leave the line — never invent a command.
- Do not remove the `DRAFT` banner, do not create a new skill, and do not add a skill pointer to
  any agent definition. The user removes the banner after reviewing.
- When you report, tell the user that removing the banner means removing **both** parts of it: the
  `> DRAFT ...` sentence and the `> Agents: this skill is NOT ready...` line. A skill left with only
  the second line is ignored by agents forever.

#### Never invent — ask, then write only from the user's answers

- **Business Context** in `CLAUDE.md`: domain, users, business constraints.
- `.caf/knowledge/golden-examples/**/RULES.md`: you may propose candidate files per pattern with
  your reasoning; the user picks them and decides the do/don't.
- `.caf/knowledge/decisions/` (ADRs): you may list the technical decisions that are visible; the
  *why* comes from the user.
- Any rule or convention the code does not already follow.

#### Hard limits

- Documents only. Do not touch application code, `package.json` or config files.
- Do not remove any `DRAFT` banner — the user removes it after reviewing.
- Do not create a document that does not exist yet without asking first.
- Do not leave a generate-time double-curly placeholder (an app-name, apps-dir or repo-mode token
  in double curly braces). The per-ticket tokens `{{TICKET-ID}}` and `{{feature-name}}` are
  intentional and must stay exactly as they are.
- Do not `git add`, commit or push. Stop in the working tree.

### 4. Verify

1. Run `caf-init curate --check-drafts` (use however `caf-init` is invoked in this environment,
   e.g. `npx caf-init`). It fails on: a tracked agent section that changed, a verification
   command whose script does not exist, a leftover placeholder, a golden-example path that does
   not exist, a `## Skills` pointer at a skill file that does not exist. Fix every `FAIL` by correcting the document — for a changed tracked section,
   restore its original text. If you cannot run it, say so and ask the user to run it.
2. Run the verification scripts you documented (lint, typecheck, test) and note the results. If
   one fails, report it — do not fix application code.
3. `git diff` must touch documents only. In `.claude/agents/*.md` your changes are limited to
   Role, Scope and Verify Checklist — a `## Skills` section there was added by
   `caf-init scaffold skills`, not by you, and must be unchanged.

### 5. Report

Briefly: files changed, `TODO`s still open and why, questions still unanswered, the
`--check-drafts` result, and anything in the code that looked inconsistent or suspicious.

# Design Ticket (Preview, Manual)

**This command is READ-MOSTLY. It may write only to `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/design.md` — DO NOT touch any application code, migrations, or schema.**

Purpose: preview technical decisions BEFORE the ticket enters the automated pipeline. Architect
is an optional role in CAF — used for tasks that involve a new schema, multiple services, or a
non-trivial architectural decision. If, after reading the ticket, the task turns out to be
simple and doesn't need an architectural decision, **say so to the user and stop** — don't
invent a design doc for a task that doesn't need one.

## Ticket

Ticket ID: `$ARGUMENTS`

REQUIRED. If empty, ask the user which ticket they mean and STOP until answered —
don't guess.

Fetch the ticket details (title, description, acceptance criteria): if an MCP tracker
(Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues) is connected, use it. Otherwise, ask the user to paste the
ticket details manually before continuing — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.

## Input

`.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` from the Planner (run `/caf-plan-ticket` first if it
doesn't exist yet, or ask the user to paste the requirements).

Optional, if available in this project — read as additional context, not a hard requirement:
- `docs/architecture/system-overview.md`
- `docs/api-contract.md`
- `docs/schema/erd.md`
- relevant ADRs in `.caf/knowledge/decisions/`

## Follow the Architect Agent's Pattern

If `.claude/agents/architect.md` exists, **read that file and follow its content as the primary
source of truth** for scope, working pattern, and output format — not the instructions in this
command. This command is just a wrapper: you run the Architect role in the main thread,
without spawning a subagent.

If that file doesn't exist, use the following default:

1. Read `requirements.md`, identify what technical decisions actually need to be made.
2. Map the components involved — **verify from the actual code structure**, don't assume
   module/service names from the ticket name.
3. For each decision: write the options considered, the choice made, and the reasoning.
   A single option with no alternative isn't an architectural decision — that's just
   ordinary implementation.
4. Check consistency with existing ADRs in `.caf/knowledge/decisions/`. If the proposed
   approach conflicts with an active ADR, say so explicitly — that needs a new ADR
   (a human decision), not a silent violation.
5. If the requirements aren't enough to make a technical decision with confidence,
   report what's missing — DO NOT guess.

## Output Format

```
design.md
## Context               ← requirements summary + why this task needs an Architect
## Affected Components   ← real files/modules/services (verified, not assumed)
## Technical Decisions
### <decision 1>
- Options considered
- Choice + reasoning
- Consequences / trade-offs
## Cross-Layer Contracts ← shape of data flowing between apps/services, if any
## Risks & Mitigations
## ADR Impact            ← which ADRs it aligns with; whether a new ADR is needed
## Open Questions        ← what can't be decided without a human answer
```

When done, show the user a brief summary: how many technical decisions were made, whether
there's any conflict with an ADR, whether there are open questions.

## Save the Output

MUST write the output to `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/design.md` — don't just display it in chat.

Before writing, check whether the target file already exists:

- **Doesn't exist** → create the folder if needed, write, continue.
- **Already exists** → DO NOT overwrite it directly. Show the user a summary of the current
  content and ask what to do: overwrite (this run's result replaces it), save as a comparison
  file, or cancel. STOP until the user answers.

## After Completion

**This command does NOT trigger `caf-orchestrator` or any automated pipeline.**
No downstream agent is spawned, no ticket status is changed, no comment/PR is posted to the
tracker. The only output is a local file in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` for a human to read.

If the user agrees with this preview and wants to proceed to the automated pipeline, they
still have to do it themselves as usual (set the ticket status to "Ready for AI" in the tracker, or whatever trigger this project uses) — remind them of this at the end of the
run, don't let the user think the pipeline has already started.

If there's an `## Open Questions` section with unanswered items, suggest the user resolve
those first before triggering the pipeline — the implementation agent will guess if the design
is left hanging, and the guess won't be caught as wrong until after the code is written.

# Discovery Start

**IMPORTANT: this command does NOT create any ticket.** Its output is a discovery document
for a human to review. Converting to a ticket is a separate command,

as input).

## 0. Permission Check (REQUIRED, before any step below)

`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission --jq .permission`

`{username}` is the user running this command — get it from `gh api user --jq .login`.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is filled in** → use it directly as the PR number, proceed to TICKET-ID

```

# Review (Initial, Pre-existing PR)

**THIS COMMAND CREATES A NEW PR REVIEW ON GITHUB.** Its side effect is real and public — a PR
Review (APPROVE/REQUEST_CHANGES/COMMENT) appears on someone else's PR timeline. This isn't a
read-only preview like `/caf-review-ticket` — only run it when you actually intend to review
this PR right now.

Purpose: the interactive path for the Reviewer Agent's INITIAL mode — reviewing from scratch a
PR that has never been reviewed by anyone (human or bot), distinct from `/caf-fix-review`
(reactive mode, responding to a human reviewer's comment on an ALREADY-reviewed PR) and distinct
from the `caf-reviewer` (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) pre-PR gate (triggered automatically in the
pipeline, not manually post-PR).

## 0. Permission Check (REQUIRED, before any step below)

`gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission --jq .permission`

`{username}` is the user running this command — obtained from `gh api user --jq .login`.
Save this `{username}` result, it's reused in step 0.7 to check for an existing review.

Result is NOT one of `write`, `maintain`, `admin` → **STOP, do not process
anything further.** NO error message to the user, NO review/comment to GitHub —
the command stops silently, only log internally if needed (e.g. one log line if there's a
mechanism for it) for an audit trail if necessary. This is not a bug, it's by design: the
CAF-PRREVIEW-01 whitelist trigger is deliberately designed to not leak to outside parties
that this command was ever invoked by an unauthorized user.

(This threshold refers to a single source: `.ai/tasks/CAF-PRREVIEW-01/plan.md` §5 — if the
threshold changes, update it there first, then here, in `/caf-fix-review`, AND on the
caf-orchestrator webhook side Checkpoint B. DO NOT update just one side.)

## 0.5 Resolve PR Number & TICKET-ID

The `$ARGUMENTS` argument is a **PR number** (e.g. `81`), **NOT a TICKET-ID** — consistent
with `/caf-fix-review`, don't mix them up.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is provided** → use it directly as the PR number, proceed to TICKET-ID
resolution below.

**`$ARGUMENTS` is empty** → auto-detect from the active branch (exact same pattern as
`/caf-fix-review` — reuse its logic, don't rewrite it differently):

```
git branch --show-current
```

- Matches pattern `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` → find its PR:
  ```
  gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --json number,url
  ```
  - Exactly one PR found → use its number, proceed.
  - No PR found for that branch → ask the user for the PR number directly, **STOP** until
    answered. Don't guess.
- Active branch does NOT match the `ai-agent/*` pattern → ask the user for the PR number
  directly, **STOP** until answered.

**TICKET-ID resolution** (needed for the `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` path — see step 1),
is DERIVED from the PR already resolved above, **not detected separately again**:

```
gh pr view {number} --json headRefName,baseRefName,url
```

Parse the `ai-agent/(.+)` pattern from the resulting `headRefName` — this regex is THE SAME
as the one used by `caf-orchestrator` (`AI_AGENT_BRANCH_PATTERN` in `run-pr-review.use-case.ts`),
keep them in sync if either side changes.

- Matches → that's the TICKET-ID.
- The PR isn't from that branch pattern (a manual PR, not the result of `/caf-run-pipeline` or
  caf-orchestrator) → ask the user for the TICKET-ID manually, **STOP** until answered. Don't make
  up a TICKET-ID from a branch name with an unclear pattern.

Save the resolved `{owner}`, `{repo}` (from `gh repo view --json owner,name`),
`{number}`, `{headRefName}`, `{baseRefName}`, and `{TICKET-ID}` — used in all
subsequent steps.

## 0.7 Check for an Existing Review (idempotency)

This command can be invoked manually even if the PR has already been reviewed before (e.g. via
the `caf-orchestrator` webhook, or a previous `/caf-review` run) — check first so reviews
don't pile up without the user's knowledge.

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews
```

Filter the result: look for an entry with `user.login == {username}` (the result resolved in
step 0 — the same user/token runs this command every time it's invoked).

- **Found a previous review from `{username}`** → show the user: timestamp
  (`submitted_at`), `state` (APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED/COMMENTED), and the old review's
  `html_url`. Ask explicitly: proceed with a new review (piling up on the PR timeline), or
  cancel? Input other than yes/no → ask again, don't guess. User chooses cancel → **STOP**, no
  side effects after this.
- **Not found** (not yet reviewed by `{username}`) → proceed silently to step 1.

Reviews from OTHER actors (other human reviewers, other bots) don't count toward this
idempotency check — not relevant to deciding "has this command already run on this PR or not".

## 1. Read Task Artifacts (optional, best-effort)

Additional context for the reviewer — path: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`:

- `requirements.md`
- `design.md`
- `verify-report.md`

Check each file with `test -f` (or read directly and catch not-found) before
assuming it exists. **Any missing folder or file → skip silently, DO NOT fail or STOP**
— a PR reviewed by this command isn't necessarily from the CAF pipeline (could be a manual PR),
so this artifact is purely optional.

## 2. Fetch the PR Diff

```
gh pr diff {number}
```

Save the result (plus `{headRefName}`, `{baseRefName}` from the 0.5 resolution) as the main
context carried into the step 3 spawn — this is what's being reviewed, not the task artifact
from step 1 (that artifact is just additional context).

## 3. Spawn `caf-reviewer` (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) — INITIAL mode

The spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not call `gh api` at all against GitHub, do not change ticket status in the tracker, do not fix any code — write `review-notes.md` only, in the usual format (Verdict, Security Audit, Qualitative Review, etc). Communicating back to GitHub (posting the PR Review) is the job of this command's main thread, done after you finish.

In addition to the prohibition above, the prompt MUST include:
- **Explicit mode: INITIAL** — a FULL review of this PR's diff from scratch, using the same
  criteria & golden examples as the usual pre-PR review (security audit checklist, qualitative
  review, verdict APPROVE/CHANGES REQUESTED/DEFER — see `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md` for the
  full format). This is NOT the `/caf-fix-review` fix-comment mode — there's no human
  reviewer comment being responded to.
- `commentContext = []` (empty array, as-is — no comments to carry over, unlike
  `/caf-fix-review` which carries thread history).
- The TICKET-ID (resolved in 0.5 — don't re-detect it here).
- The PR diff from step 2, plus the task artifact from step 1 if present (leave that section
  empty in the prompt if it genuinely wasn't found, don't pretend it exists).
- Instructions to write `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md` — format EXACTLY as defined
  in `.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md` (Ticket, Agent, Verdict, Security Audit, Qualitative Review,
  Verdict Rationale, For Developer) — **don't invent a new structure**, reuse the existing one.

Wait for the spawn to finish before proceeding to step 4.

## 4. Post GitHub PR Review

Read `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md` from step 3. Take the `Verdict` from it,
map it to a GitHub PR Review `event` (this mapping is this command's own decision, NOT
defined in `caf-reviewer.md`):

| Verdict (review-notes.md) | GitHub `event` |
|---|---|
| APPROVE | `APPROVE` |
| CHANGES REQUESTED | `REQUEST_CHANGES` |
| DEFER | `COMMENT` |

A verdict OTHER than these three (e.g. `NEEDS_HUMAN` — that value is defined in
`caf-reviewer.md` for the pipeline's automatic retry cycle, NOT for this single-run manual
command) or capitalization/spelling that doesn't match exactly → **STOP**, show the raw
`Verdict` to the user, ask which GitHub event to use manually. Don't guess or default
silently to `COMMENT`.

`body` = a summary of `review-notes.md` (Verdict Rationale + a concise list of
Blockers/Non-blockers — not the entire raw file pasted in, but complete enough that a human
reviewer doesn't have to open the file to get the gist).

`comments[]` (optional) — if `review-notes.md` has findings with a specific `path`+`line`
that can be mapped to the PR diff (e.g. from a Security Audit section naming a specific file),
include them as per-file inline comments:

```
gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{number}/reviews -X POST \
  -f event="{APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES|COMMENT}" \
  -f body="{summary}" \
  -f 'comments[][path]=...' -f 'comments[][line]=...' -f 'comments[][body]=...'
```

(or a JSON payload via `--input -` if there's more than one `comments[]` entry — pick
whichever approach is valid for multiple comments, don't assume there's only one.)

Findings without a clear `path`+`line` (general, qualitative concerns) → go into `body`
only, don't force them into an inline comment.

**If the `gh api` call above fails with `422 Unprocessable Entity`** — check the
`errors[]` field in the response:

- Contains `"Can not approve your own pull request"` (event `APPROVE`) OR
  `"Can not request changes on your own pull request"` (event `REQUEST_CHANGES`) — confirmed
  empirically (PR #83/GAN-114, 2026-08-22): the GitHub API rejects both of these events when the
  user running the command (the `gh` token) is the same as the PR author, with a different
  message per event, not one generic message. `COMMENT` is NOT subject to this restriction
  (confirmed to succeed when posting on your own PR). → **STOP, don't retry automatically with
  a different event.** Show the user: this PR is authored by the same user running the
  command — the GitHub API rejected `{original event}` for their own PR. Offer two explicit
  options, let the user choose (don't default to either):
  1. **Post as `COMMENT`** — `body` MUST start with an explicit statement of the actual
     verdict on the first line, e.g.: `"⚠ Actual verdict: {APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES} — posted as
     COMMENT because the GitHub API rejected self-{approve|request-changes}."`, followed by the
     usual summary. **Don't silently downgrade** — this statement must actually appear in the
     body that gets posted, not just be noted in a local log.
  2. **Cancel** — no PR Review gets posted. Suggest the user ask another reviewer/token to run
     the command.
- `errors[]` does NOT match either pattern above (some other cause — e.g. PR already
  closed/merged, malformed `comments[]`) → **STOP as usual**, show the raw error message to the
  user. Don't assume this is a self-review case.

## 5. Summary to the User

Show in chat: the final Verdict, the GitHub event used, a link to the newly created PR Review
(from the step 4 `gh api` response), and the location of `review-notes.md` for full details.

## Constraints

- This command NEVER runs `git push`, NEVER checks out/commits code, NEVER changes ticket
  status in the tracker — the only writes are `review-notes.md` (subagent) and the new
  PR Review on GitHub (main thread, step 4).
- The idempotency check (step 0.7) ONLY detects a previous `/caf-review` run (whether from
  this command itself, from the same `{username}`). **CAF-ORCH-PRREVIEW-03 (caf-orchestrator,
  2026-09-04)**: the webhook's mode `initial` now runs the same real INITIAL (Verdict-producing)
  contract as this command and posts via `pulls/{number}/reviews` too (`RunPrReviewUseCase` →
  `IVcsClient.createPullRequestReview`) — the artifact-contract mismatch that used to make
  `GET pulls/{number}/reviews` blind to the webhook's review is gone. What's **STILL NOT
  detected**: actor-login mismatch — this step filters by `user.login == {username}` (the human
  running this command), but the webhook posts under the pipeline's own bot/token login, so a
  prior webhook-triggered review still won't match here even though it now exists as the same
  kind of PR Review object. Genuine remaining gap, tracked separately (not in
  CAF-ORCH-PRREVIEW-03's scope, which explicitly excluded it) — see
  `.ai/tasks/CAF-PRREVIEW-01/open-items.md` (caf-initiator).
- Inline `comments[]` (step 4) depends on `review-notes.md` naming an explicit
  `path`+`line` for its findings — if the reviewer only gives a general concern without a
  clear location, the review still gets posted but without an inline comment (it all goes into
  the `body` summary).
- This Checkpoint A (caf-initiator) isn't yet wired to an automatic webhook — this command is
  always triggered manually by the user. Automatic triggering for a new PR (e.g. fired on the
  `opened` event) is caf-orchestrator's scope, outside this command.
- This command CANNOT produce a PR Review with event `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES`
  if the user running the command is the author of the PR being reviewed — this is a
  restriction from the GitHub API itself (confirmed empirically, PR #83/GAN-114, 2026-08-22:
  both are rejected with `422` and a different message per event), not a bug in this command.
  The available fallback (see step 4): post as `COMMENT` with the actual verdict stated
  explicitly on the first line of the `body`, or cancel entirely — the command never silently
  downgrades the event without user confirmation.

# Run Pipeline (Manual, No Orchestrator)

**This command WRITES CODE and CREATES A BRANCH.** It's the only command generated by
caf-initiator that does both — treat it more carefully than the others.

Purpose: a manual alternative for projects that haven't set up (or don't want) `caf-orchestrator`
(webhook + VPS). The flow mirrors the automated pipeline, including **auto-commit, auto-push, and
auto `gh pr create`** after Reviewer APPROVE — see section 7. No ticket status is changed in the
tracker (that stays manual); only git + PR are automated.

**If it stops at NEEDS_HUMAN** (implementation, QA gate, or Reviewer gate): there is NO commit,
push, or PR at all — the working tree is left as-is on branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` for a human.
See "Controlled Stop" below.

Boundary worth knowing: the `allowed-tools` allowlist above binds this command (MAIN THREAD),
**not the spawned subagents** — subagents run with the tools from their own agent definition.
That's why every spawn prompt below MUST explicitly include the push/PR prohibition ("that's the
main thread's job in section 7, not yours") — commit/push/PR may happen only once, in section 7,
performed by the main thread after all gates pass.

## Ticket

Ticket ID: `$ARGUMENTS`

Required. If empty, ask the user which ticket is meant and STOP until answered — don't guess.

Fetch ticket details (title, description, acceptance criteria): if a tracker MCP is connected
(Linear/Jira/GitHub Issues), use it. Otherwise, ask the user to paste the ticket details manually
before continuing — don't invent requirements that weren't stated.

## 0. Guard — required, before spawning anything

Run these four checks **sequentially and to completion** before the Task tool is used at all.
Don't spawn any agent "while waiting for the user's answer".

### 0.1 Working directory must be clean

`git status --porcelain`. If there's output (uncommitted changes) → **STOP**, show the list, ask
the user to commit/stash first. Don't check out a new branch with changes that could get carried
along or lost.

### 0.2 Does branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` already exist?

Check **both local AND remote** — both, not just one:

```
git branch --list ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
git ls-remote --heads origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

Checking remote isn't a formality: `caf-orchestrator` runs on a VPS, so if it has already/is
currently handling this ticket, its branch shows up on the **remote** and may not exist in the
user's working copy at all. A local-only check would pass exactly in the most dangerous case.

If this repo has no `origin` remote at all (`git ls-remote` fails with "'origin' does not appear
to be a git repository"), that's **not a guard failure** — a purely local repo simply can't be
claimed by the orchestrator. Note "remote: none", proceed with the local check result only. Don't
STOP because of this, and don't treat the remote check as passed either.

- **Not present in either** → proceed to 0.3.
- **Present in either/both** → **STOP**. This is a strong signal this ticket is already/currently
  being handled by the orchestrator or a previous `/caf-run-pipeline` run. Show the user:
  - `git log --oneline` for that branch (whatever commits already exist there),
  - the contents of `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md` if it exists,
  - whether it was local, remote, or both.

  Then ask for explicit confirmation: **continue on that branch**, or **abort**. DO NOT assume
  it's safe to continue, and DO NOT create a new branch that overwrites it. If the user chooses
  to continue, `git checkout ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` (not `-b`).

  **Limitation you must disclose to the user at this point:** an orchestrator run that just
  started and hasn't pushed its branch yet is NOT detected by this check. If the user knows an
  automated pipeline is currently running for this ticket, abort — regardless of the check
  results above.

### 0.3 Already completed before?

Check `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/verify-report.md`.

If that file exists and its status is **not** `NEEDS_HUMAN` → **STOP**. This ticket has likely
already been completed. Show its summary, ask the user: **restart from scratch (override)** or
**abort**. Don't silently overwrite completed work.

Deliberately phrased as "not NEEDS_HUMAN" rather than "equals SUCCESS": the success label in
`verify-report.md` isn't consistent across sources (CAF.md calls it `SUCCESS`, the handoff
template calls it `PASS`, and agents in the wild sometimes write `DONE`). The only consistent
marker is `NEEDS_HUMAN` for "not yet done". Matching the exact string `SUCCESS` would make this
guard silently never fire — exactly the failure it's meant to prevent.

If the status is `NEEDS_HUMAN`, don't STOP: this ticket was genuinely left unfinished. Tell the
user this run continues previously interrupted work, then proceed.

### 0.4 Create the branch

Only after 0.1-0.3 pass: `git checkout -b ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` from the currently active branch.
If the user already chose "continue" in 0.2, the branch is already checked out — skip this step.

## 1. Planner (required)

Spawn Planner. Its source of truth is `.claude/agents/caf-planner.md` — read that file and follow
it. Input: ticket details from the Ticket section above.

Required output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/requirements.md` and `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/tasks.md`.

If Planner reports the ticket is too ambiguous to break down, **STOP the entire pipeline** —
report to the user and ask for ticket clarification. Don't proceed to implementation with a plan
Planner itself says it isn't confident about.

## 2. Architect (conditional)

This stage is **conditional** — don't always spawn it.

Spawn Architect (`.claude/agents/caf-architect.md`) ONLY if either is true:

- `tasks.md` from Planner explicitly states it needs an architecture/design decision, OR
- the task touches more than one app/service, OR involves a new schema/migration.

If the ticket is simple and single-app, **skip** — go on to stage 3. Producing `design.md`
for a task that doesn't need it just adds run cost and a document nobody reads.

Output: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/design.md`. If skipped, note in the final summary that this
stage was skipped along with the reason — don't let it silently disappear from the report.

## 3. Implementation

Implementation agents available in this project:

- `caf-implementer` (`.claude/agents/caf-implementer.md`)

**How to choose which agent to spawn** (this decision must NOT be guessed):

1. Read the app/module column of each task in `tasks.md`.
2. Match it against each agent's scope above — read `## Scope` in the agent's file, don't
   guess from its name.
3. A task whose app/module matches one agent's scope → that agent handles it.
4. If a task doesn't match any agent's scope, OR matches more than one, **ask the user**
   which agent should handle it and STOP until answered.
   Misrouting means an agent writes code outside its scope — a silent failure only caught at
   review time.
5. An agent with no tasks at all: DO NOT spawn it. Not a failure — there's simply no work for
   it on this ticket.

If multiple agents have tasks, run them **sequentially, not in parallel** — both write to the
same working tree. Order follows the task dependencies in `tasks.md`.

Input for each agent: `requirements.md`, `tasks.md`, and `design.md` if stage 2 ran.

Every spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours. Write only the code and
> `verify-report.md`, on the branch that's already active.

**Internal PIV is that agent's own concern.** Implementation agents already have their own Retry
Logic (implement → verify → fix, max 3x) in their definition. You are **NOT** allowed to respawn
an implementation agent just because its verify failed — that would effectively double the retry
budget. The only respawn path is the gate retries in stages 5 and 6.

If an agent finishes with `verify-report.md` `Status: NEEDS_HUMAN`:
**STOP the entire pipeline here.** Don't proceed to Documentation/QA/Reviewer with code whose
verify hasn't passed — every subsequent stage would produce a report about code already known to
be broken, and that's wasted cost.

## 4. Documentation (non-blocking)

Spawn Documentation (`.claude/agents/caf-documentation.md`) to update the documentation to match
the changes already written.

The spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**This stage is NON-BLOCKING.** By CAF design, Documentation is not a gate: if this agent
fails, declines, or concludes there's no documentation to change — **do not stop the
pipeline**. Record the outcome as one line in the final summary and continue to the QA stage.

Do not retry this stage. There is no retry budget for a non-blocking stage.

## 5. QA (gate)

The QA (`.claude/agents/caf-qa.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `qaRetryCount`, `MAX_QA_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `qaRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn QA (`.claude/agents/caf-qa.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `NEEDS_HUMAN / has a CRITICAL issue`:
   - If `qaRetryCount >= MAX_QA_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `qaRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `qa-report.md` as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`qaRetryCount >= MAX_QA_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

A `NON-CRITICAL` issue found by QA does NOT fail the gate — that's intentional, not an
overlooked gap. If QA closes with `## Status: PASS` while the `### NON-CRITICAL` section in
`qa-report.md` is non-empty, treat it as "Result OK" and proceed to the next stage. Those
findings stay recorded in `qa-report.md` to be addressed separately — outside this retry loop.
Only `## Status: NEEDS_HUMAN` or content in the `### CRITICAL` section triggers the retry
gate.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/qa-report.md`.

## 6. Reviewer (gate)

The Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`) spawn prompt MUST include, verbatim:

> Do not `git push`, do not open a PR, do not change the ticket status in the tracker — that is the main thread's job in section 7, not yours.

**Gate — `reviewerRetryCount`, `MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES = 1`.**

Set `reviewerRetryCount = 0` at the start of this run. This counter is **fresh every time
`/caf-run-pipeline` runs** and **independent** of other gate counters — budget exhausted on
one gate does NOT reduce another gate's budget. Don't treat it as a shared budget.

Flow:

1. Spawn Reviewer (`.claude/agents/caf-reviewer.md`), wait for its result.
2. Result OK → proceed to the next stage.
3. Result `REQUEST_CHANGES / NEEDS_HUMAN`:
   - If `reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES` → **STOP here**, report NEEDS_HUMAN (see
     "Controlled Stop" below).
   - Otherwise → increment `reviewerRetryCount` by 1 from its previous value, then **respawn the
     relevant implementation agent** with `review-notes.md` (BLOCKING findings only) as input, asking it to fix only the
     findings (not redo the implementation from scratch). Once the fix is done, run this gate
     **once more**, back to step 1.
4. Budget exhausted (`reviewerRetryCount >= MAX_REVIEWER_RETRIES`) and the gate still fails → STOP,
   NEEDS_HUMAN.

Retry means **fix, then re-check** — not running the gate twice over the exact same code.
Re-running the gate with nothing changed just burns cost for a result that's already certain to
be the same.

Artifact: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md`.

To be explicit: `reviewerRetryCount` is **not affected** by what happens in the QA stage. A
ticket whose QA passed after a retry still enters this stage with a full budget of 1.

## 7. Commit, Push, PR (SUCCESS)

**This stage runs ONLY if Reviewer APPROVEs.** If the pipeline stopped at any stage before this
(implementation NEEDS_HUMAN, QA/Reviewer gate exhausted), **skip this entire section** and go
straight to "Controlled Stop" below — don't commit anything.

Run these seven steps **in order**. Any step with a STOP condition must halt there, not proceed
to the next step — a commit with the wrong scope or a push that collides with the remote branch
can't easily be undone once it happens.

### 7.1 Scope whitelist

Paths allowed into the commit (ONLY these, not the entire working tree):

- `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/` (artifact)
- `caf-implementer`: the whole repository (single-package repo, no per-app split)
- `caf-documentation`: `README.md`
- `caf-documentation`: `CHANGELOG.md`
- `caf-documentation`: `docs/`

`docs/` is whitelisted as one whole folder (not a specific subpath) because the Documentation
agent has no granular path scope — this means the scope check in 7.1 can't distinguish what the
Documentation agent wrote from other files that happen to be written to `docs/` by another
process in the same run.

`git status --porcelain` → match **every** changed path against the whitelist above.

A path changed BUT not in any whitelist → **STOP, DO NOT commit anything**. Show the suspicious
paths to the user, explain this is likely a file outside the assigned agent's scope (a bug or
scope creep in a subagent). Ask the user to decide manually — commit anyway after verifying, or
investigate first. In the Final Summary, record the status as "SUCCESS but commit aborted —
scope drift detected", not a plain SUCCESS status.

### 7.2 Commit

`git add --` followed by the explicit list of paths from 7.1 that actually changed (**not**
`git add -A`), then:

```
git commit -m "AI agent pipeline: {TICKET-ID}"
```

Without `--allow-empty`. If the commit fails because there's nothing to commit ("nothing to
commit") — that's an odd signal (implementation reported done but there's no diff at all) →
**STOP**, report to the user, don't proceed to push/PR.

### 7.3 Guard — fetch before push

```
git fetch origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

If fetch fails because the branch doesn't exist on the remote at all, that's not a guard
failure — proceed treating it as "remote doesn't exist yet" (next step).

- **Remote doesn't exist** → safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} HEAD`
  succeeds (exit 0) → the remote SHA is an ancestor of local HEAD, safe, proceed to 7.4.
- **Remote exists**, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor` fails (exit != 0) → the remote SHA is
  NOT an ancestor of local HEAD. **STOP before pushing.** This signals the remote branch has been
  changed by another party (the orchestrator, or another `/caf-run-pipeline` run) since guard
  0.2 ran at the start of this command. Show the user: the remote SHA, `git log --oneline` of
  that remote branch, and the local commit just created in 7.2 (still in the working tree, not
  yet pushed). **DO NOT force-push, DO NOT auto merge/rebase** — that's a human decision.

**Limitation to disclose to the user at this point**: this is best-effort, not an absolute
guarantee — a race condition between this fetch-check and the push in 7.4 is still possible
(small window, but real) if another party pushes exactly between the two steps. There's no
distributed lock available from this command's side to close that gap entirely — same pattern of
limitation as guard 0.2.

### 7.4 Push

```
git push --set-upstream origin ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}
```

### 7.5 Detect base branch

```
gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef --jq .defaultBranchRef.name
```

Save the result as `{BASE-BRANCH}`. **Don't hardcode `main`** — the target repo might use
`master`, `develop`, or another name.

### 7.6 Check for an existing PR (idempotency)

```
gh pr list --head ai-agent/{TICKET-ID} --state open --json url,number
```

- **Result found** → a PR for this branch already exists (e.g. opened manually by the user after
  a previous NEEDS_HUMAN run, and now the follow-up run succeeded). **Don't** call
  `gh pr create` — the push in 7.4 already updates the branch underlying that PR. Take the URL
  from the `gh pr list` result, note it for the Final Summary as "PR already exists, branch
  updated" — not an error.
- **Empty** → proceed to 7.7.

### 7.7 `gh pr create`

Title:
```

```

Body — structure identical to `buildPrBody` in caf-orchestrator (`run-agent-pipeline.use-case.ts`),
so both execution paths produce the same PR shape:

- QA: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/qa-report.md`
- Review: `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/review-notes.md`

{docsNote — Documentation status from stage 4: SUCCESS / FAILED (non-blocking) / NOT AVAILABLE,
the equivalent wording already used in the Final Summary}

{raw contents of review-notes.md}
```

No skip-gate warning block (`qualityGateWarning` in the orchestrator) — this command has no

Base: `{BASE-BRANCH}` from 7.5. Save the URL returned by `gh pr create` for the Final Summary.

## Controlled Stop (NEEDS_HUMAN)

If any gate exhausts its budget, or implementation ends in NEEDS_HUMAN: that's a **controlled
stop, not an error**. Don't throw an exception, don't make the command look like it "crashed",
don't try an alternative path not instructed here.

What to do: stop at that stage, go straight to the Final Summary with status NEEDS_HUMAN and
state which stage stopped it plus what findings remain unresolved. Code already written stays on
the branch — don't revert it, don't delete it. A human decides whether to continue or discard it.

**To be explicit: the NEEDS_HUMAN path never reaches section 7.** There is no commit, push, or PR
at all on this path — the working tree is left exactly as the last stage that stopped the
pipeline left it. This isn't new behavior (it's already implied by the stop/`return` structure
in each gate), written explicitly here to remove ambiguity.

- [ ] The currently active branch really is `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}` (`git branch --show-current`)
- [ ] The artifact for every stage that ran actually exists in `.caf/tasks/{TICKET-ID}/`
- [ ] **No push happened** — `git status -sb`: the first line must not mention an upstream

**If the run ended SUCCESS (section 7 ran):**

- [ ] A push actually happened — `git status -sb` mentions the upstream
      `origin/ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`
- [ ] The PR exists — either newly created in 7.7 OR an existing one detected in 7.6, its URL is
      correct and reachable
- [ ] `git show --stat HEAD` — every path in the latest commit is indeed in the 7.1 whitelist, no

## Final Summary

Show a status table for every stage:

```
| Stage          | Status                          | Artifact |
| Planner        | SUCCESS                         | requirements.md, tasks.md |
| Architect      | SUCCESS / SKIP (reason)         | design.md |
| Implementation | SUCCESS / NEEDS_HUMAN           | verify-report.md |
| Documentation  | SUCCESS / FAILED (non-blocking) / NOT AVAILABLE | - |
| QA             | PASS (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | qa-report.md |
| Reviewer       | APPROVE (retry: n/1) / NEEDS_HUMAN / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | review-notes.md |
| Commit/Push/PR | SUCCESS (new/existing PR) / ABORTED (scope drift) / NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped) | commit + PR URL |
```

A stage that was **never invoked** because the pipeline already stopped before reaching it (e.g.
QA exhausted → Reviewer never spawned) is filled in as `NOT RUN (a prior stage stopped)`.
**Never** fill in `NEEDS_HUMAN` for a stage that was never executed — that implies the stage
ran and found a problem, when it didn't. Its artifact doesn't exist either, so write `-` in the
Artifact column.

State the final `qaRetryCount` and `reviewerRetryCount` as-is — that tells the user how
smoothly this run went.

**SUCCESS** (section 7 completed):

> Code committed, pushed to `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`, PR: {PR URL from 7.6/7.7}.

**NEEDS_HUMAN**:

> Code is on branch `ai-agent/{TICKET-ID}`, not committed/pushed. Continue or fix it manually,
> then re-run `/caf-run-pipeline {TICKET-ID}` when ready — guard 0.2/0.3 above will detect the
